subject: Spanska
title: Grammar: past tense (pretérito)
sourceSummary: The basics of the pretérito (past tense) for regular -ar, -er, and -ir verbs, plus the common irregular verbs ser/ir and hacer.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Ayer yo ___ con mis amigos." (hablar = to talk)
questions.opener: -ar verbs in the preterite end in -é for "yo".
questions.explanation: Preterite of -ar verbs: hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablasteis, hablaron. "Yo" gives the ending -é: "hablé" (I talked).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Ella ___ una carta la semana pasada." (escribir = to write)
questions.opener: -ir verbs in the preterite end in -ió for "él/ella".
questions.explanation: Preterite of -ir verbs: escribí, escribiste, escribió, escribimos, escribisteis, escribieron. "Ella" gives "escribió" (she wrote).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "El año pasado nosotros ___ a España." (ir = to go)
questions.opener: Ir is completely irregular in the preterite — and actually shares its form with ser!
questions.explanation: Preterite of "ir": fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. "Nosotros" gives "fuimos" (we went). The same form is actually used for "ser" in the preterite.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "¿Qué ___ tú anoche?" (hacer = to do)
questions.opener: Hacer is irregular in the preterite: hice, hiciste...
questions.explanation: Preterite of "hacer": hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicisteis, hicieron. "Tú" gives "hiciste" (you did).

questions.prompt: Which time expression best fits with the preterite?
questions.opener: The preterite describes completed events at a specific point in time.
questions.explanation: "Ayer" (yesterday) points to a completed event at a specific point in time, which is exactly what the preterite is used for. The other expressions describe recurring habits and fit better with the present tense.

questions.prompt: Write the preterite form of "comer" (to eat) for "tú": "Tú ___ mucho en la fiesta."
questions.opener: -er verbs follow the same preterite pattern as -ir verbs.

questions.prompt: Correct the two errors: "Ayer yo comi pizza y despues yo hablo con mi amiga por teléfono."
questions.opener: Two verbs that should both be in the preterite, not the present.
questions.answer: Ayer yo comí pizza y después yo hablé con mi amiga por teléfono.
steps: "Comi" is missing the accent and is the wrong form: "comí" (with an accent on the i) is the correct preterite form for "I ate".
"Hablo" is present tense ("I talk"), but since it's about yesterday it should be preterite: "hablé" (I talked).
The full sentence: "Ayer yo comí pizza y después yo hablé con mi amiga por teléfono."

questions.prompt: How are regular verbs and the most common irregular verbs conjugated in the preterite?
questions.opener: Past tense forms for completed events, plus three important irregular verbs.
questions.answer: -ar (hablar): hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablasteis, hablaron. -er/-ir (comer/escribir): comí/escribí, comiste/escribiste, comió/escribió, comimos/escribimos, comisteis/escribisteis, comieron/escribieron. Ir/ser (same form!): fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. Hacer: hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicisteis, hicieron. Time expressions that fit: ayer (yesterday), la semana pasada (last week), el año pasado (last year), anoche (last night).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Vosotros ___ mucho en la fiesta." (bailar = to dance)
questions.opener: "Vosotros" (you all) in the preterite for -ar verbs ends in -asteis.
questions.explanation: Preterite of -ar verbs: bailé, bailaste, bailó, bailamos, bailasteis, bailaron. "Vosotros" gives "bailasteis".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Ellos ___ la puerta antes de salir." (cerrar = to close)
questions.opener: "Ellos" (they) in the preterite for -ar verbs ends in -aron.
questions.explanation: Preterite of -ar verbs: cerré, cerraste, cerró, cerramos, cerrasteis, cerraron. "Ellos" gives "cerraron".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form of "ser" in the preterite: "Ese día ___ muy especial." (That day was very special.)
questions.opener: "Ese día" (that day) corresponds to the he/she/it form.
questions.explanation: Preterite of "ser": fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. "Ese día" (that day) gives "fue".

questions.prompt: What is the preterite form of "tener" for "yo"?
questions.opener: "Tener" has an irregular stem "tuv-" in the preterite.
questions.explanation: Preterite of "tener": tuve, tuviste, tuvo, tuvimos, tuvisteis, tuvieron. "Yo" gives "tuve".

questions.prompt: Which time expression does NOT fit with the preterite?
questions.opener: Think about which expression describes a recurring habit rather than a completed event.
questions.explanation: "Todos los días" (every day) describes a recurring habit and fits better with the present or imperfect tense, not the preterite, which describes completed events at a specific point in time.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form of "poder" (to be able to) in the preterite: "Yo no ___ venir a la fiesta." (I couldn't come to the party.)
questions.opener: "Poder" has an irregular stem "pud-" in the preterite.
questions.explanation: Preterite of "poder": pude, pudiste, pudo, pudimos, pudisteis, pudieron. "Yo" gives "pude".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "¿___ (tú) la película anoche?" (ver = to see)
questions.opener: "Ver" is irregular but follows a simple pattern in the preterite.
questions.explanation: Preterite of "ver": vi, viste, vio, vimos, visteis, vieron. "Tú" gives "viste".
